_law: STAGE 3 -- STATE VARIANTS. A variant is a REPAINT of the same plate, not a filter (CONTENT-full.md 6.2: room-dim.jpg is the painted relight the insets dim to, and the actors standing in it go through the same relight as a measured colour matrix). Every candidate here is image-to-image off assets/plates/book/church/church.jpg and is accepted only if tools/laneassets/platediff.py says the change was confined to what it was allowed to touch.
_ruling_on_scope: The scene ledger's `church` table names two variants, church.jpg and church-dim.jpg. The lane brief asked whether the ring moment wants one too. RULING: yes for the LIGHT, no for the GEOMETRY. Unit 9's act is `ringScrub` 0->1 over 4.5 s and its cameo caption flips to IRENE NORTON -- the chapter's one change of identity -- so the altar has to CHANGE, visibly, on that beat. But the hourglass (act glassStart) and the sovereign (act sovereignScrub) are named FREE LAYERS in the ledger, and the four figures are named ACTOR layers; those get layer states, not plate repaints, because a plate repaint cannot be moved and they must move. So exactly one dramatic variant is generated: church-ring.

variants.intent: The painted relight the raised plates dim to. Judged on EDGE IOU, not on changed-pixel percentage: a relight moves every pixel and keeps every edge, so a high IoU is the proof it was relit rather than re-rendered. Beat I's measured matrix is 0.448/0.588/0.754 -- red falls hardest, blue survives -- and this variant is asked for the same behaviour so the two SETs dim alike.
variants.prompt:
RELIGHT THIS PICTURE. DO NOT REDRAW IT. Every wall, window, pew, candlestick, figure, roof beam and rock facet must stay in EXACTLY the same place, at exactly the same size, with exactly the same shape and the same faceted low-poly geometry. This is a lighting change only.

THE CHANGE: the whole picture becomes much darker and cooler, as if it had been dimmed down behind glass. Take the candle flames and the warm amber light on the chancel down hard -- the warm glow on the plaster should almost go out, leaving only a faint ember of it. Let the cool moonlit blue of the lancet windows and the nave survive better than the warm light does: the picture should end up clearly BLUER and much less orange than it started. Deep shadows go nearly black. The dark navy background void stays as it is.

Keep it a painting of the same model from the same camera: same framing, same composition, same edges, same silhouettes, no new objects, nothing removed, nothing moved. No text, no letters, no writing.

variants.intent: Unit 9, `iv-09-tyingup`. The instant the ring goes on. The change must be a LIGHT event at the joined hands and on the altar top, not a re-pose: the three figures are the plate's rest state (fact M.1) and moving them here would break every actor mark the next lane measures off this plate. Diff-gated hard -- outside the box is a leak.
variants.prompt:
CHANGE ONE SMALL THING IN THIS PICTURE AND NOTHING ELSE.

WHAT CHANGES: the bride and the groom are standing with their near hands joined low in front of them, between them, just above waist height. At that exact spot -- where their two hands meet -- add a small, bright, warm GOLD glint: a wedding ring catching the candlelight, with a tight warm golden halo around it about the size of a thumbnail, and a soft warm gold light falling on both of their joined hands and on the cuffs at their wrists. Let a little of that same warm gold spill onto the altar cloth to their right, so the altar top reads a shade warmer and brighter than before.

WHAT MUST NOT CHANGE: everything else. Do not move, re-pose, re-shape or re-colour the bride, the groom or the clergyman -- same stance, same arms, same heads, same clothes, same faces. Do not touch the walls, the two lancet windows, the big east window, the roof beams, the pews, the floor, the crimson runner, the altar rail, the candlesticks, the hourglass, the flower, the rock base or the dark navy background. Same camera, same framing, same faceted low-poly style, same overall exposure. No text, no letters, no writing.
